correctness.rationale: For each rational projective line, substituting the line into C_{q,k} divides by the Fermat factor s^qt−st^q with q+1 simple rational roots; the residual binary quadratic is nonzero. On W=1 and V=1 dual charts its discriminant is 4Delta_k, with the missing line X=0 separately handled. Thus discriminant zero gives exactly one rational flex contact (multiplicity 3); otherwise either zero or two rational order-2 contacts. Independently checked both chart discriminant identities symbolically. The quartic Delta=UW³+V³W−kUVW²−kV⁴−U³V has no singularities at infinity. Singular equations in characteristic 3 exclude finite singularities; in other odd characteristics they correspond exactly to multiple roots of T⁷+kT³−1. A root-free polynomial over F_q is squarefree here because any multiple root is F_q-rational (special case char7 included). Hence D_k smooth genus3. Incidence counts with all q²+q+1 rational points smooth yield N1=#D(Fq), N0=N2=(q²+q+1−#D)/2. Hasse–Weil gives |N2−q²/2|<=3sqrt q.
residual_risks: The original curve C is not claimed geometrically smooth; contacts are only at F_q-rational smooth points. Symbolic checks do not prove universal squarefreeness without the displayed eliminations.

The inspected full primary text does not identify the smooth genus-three dual quartic, rational flex/two-contact line classification or Weil-scale count. The two-chart quadratic discriminant and singularity-to-G_k link supply nontrivial geometry not just a trivial substitution. Resultary comparisons returned unrelated quartic singularities and plane dual-degree work.
